results.title: Amenable group (Følner condition)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A discrete group $G$ is *amenable* if it satisfies the Følner condition: for every finite subset $K \subseteq G$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a finite nonempty subset $F \subseteq G$ such that $|sF \mathbin{\triangle} F| / |F| < \varepsilon$ for every $s \in K$. Here $sF = \{sf : f \in F\}$ is the left translate of $F$ by $s$, $\triangle$ is symmetric difference and $|\cdot|$ is cardinality.

results.title: Finite groups are amenable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite group is amenable.

results.title: Trivial groups are amenable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every group with at most one element is amenable; the set $F = \{1\}$ witnesses the Følner condition.

results.title: $k$-full numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A natural number $n$ is $k$-full if $n \ne 0$ and $p^k$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.

results.title: Powerful part of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$ and a prime $p$, let $v_p(n)$ be the exponent of $p$ in $n$. The powerful (or $2$-full) part of $n$ is the product of the prime powers $p^{v_p(n)}$ over the primes $p$ dividing $n$ with $v_p(n) \ge 2$ (and $1$ if there are none). The powerful part of $0$ is defined to be $1$.

results.title: Prime exponents of the powerful part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $p$, write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $n$ (it is $0$ when $p$ is not a prime factor of $n$). Then the exponent of $p$ in the powerful part of $n$ equals $v_p(n)$ if $v_p(n) \ge 2$, and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: The powerful part of $n$ divides $n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the powerful part of $n$ divides $n$.

results.title: Factorization criterion for $k$-full numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n \ne 0$, and write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of a prime $p$ in the prime factorization of $n$. Then $n$ is $k$-full if and only if $k \le v_p(n)$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.

results.title: Zero is not $k$-full
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $0$ is not $k$-full.

results.title: One is $k$-full
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $1$ is $k$-full: it is nonzero and has no prime divisors.

results.title: The $0$-full numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is $0$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$, since $p^0 = 1$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$.

results.title: The $1$-full numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is $1$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$, since $p^1 = p$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.

results.title: Monotonicity of $k$-fullness in $k$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $j \le k$ be natural numbers. Every $k$-full natural number is $j$-full.

results.title: For $k \ge 2$, $k$-full numbers are $2$-full
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number. Every $k$-full natural number is $2$-full.

results.title: The $2$-full numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is $2$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$ and $p^2$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$. These are the squarefull (also called powerful) numbers.

results.title: Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathbb{R}^n$ denotes the real Euclidean space of dimension $n$: real vectors with coordinates indexed by $0, \dots, n-1$, with the Euclidean inner product and norm.

results.title: Partial derivative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a coordinate index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a function $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the partial derivative $\partial_i \varphi$ is the function $\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ sending $x$ to $D\varphi(x)(e_i)$, the Fréchet derivative of $\varphi$ at $x$ applied to the $i$-th standard basis vector $e_i$. At points where $\varphi$ is not differentiable its value is $0$.

results.title: Mixed partial derivative

results.title: Sobolev space $W^{k,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Sobolev embedding theorem (Morrey regime)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n, k, r$ be natural numbers and $\alpha, p$ real numbers with $n < p$, $0 < \alpha \le 1$ and $r + \alpha < k - n/p$. results.title: Set arithmetic progressions with given first term and difference
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and $a, d \in M$. A set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ with first term $a$ and difference $d$ if $s = \{a + n d : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$ and $s$ has exactly $l$ elements, counting the size of an infinite set as $\infty$; here $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.

results.title: Sets that are arithmetic progressions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A set $s \subseteq \alpha$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ if there are $a, d \in \alpha$ such that $s = \{a + nd : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$ and $s$ has exactly $l$ elements (infinitely many when $l = \infty$). Here $nd$ denotes the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.

results.title: Cardinality of a set arithmetic progression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If a set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then $s$ has exactly $l$ elements, counting the size of an infinite set as $\infty$.

results.title: First term and difference of a set arithmetic progression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If a set $s \subseteq M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then there are $a, d \in M$ with $s = \{a + n d : n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < l\}$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.

results.title: List arithmetic progressions with given start and difference
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $l \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a, d \in M$. A list $s$ of elements of $M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ starting from $a$ with difference $d$, in either direction, if $s = (a, a + d, \dots, a + (l - 1)d)$ or $s = (a + (l - 1)d, \dots, a + d, a)$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$; when $l = 0$ both lists are empty.

results.title: Arithmetic progressions of lists
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N}$. A list $s$ of elements of $M$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ if there are $a, d \in M$ such that $s = (a, a + d, \dots, a + (l - 1)d)$ or $s = (a + (l - 1)d, \dots, a + d, a)$, where $n d$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $d$.

results.title: Monotone arithmetic progressions in a function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $\beta$ a preordered type, $f : \beta \to M$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ contains a monotone arithmetic progression of length $k$ if there are $x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_k$ in $\beta$ such that the list $(f(x_1), \dots, f(x_k))$ is an arithmetic progression of length $k$: for some $a, d \in M$ it equals $(a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1)d)$ or its reverse.

results.title: Progression-free sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A set $s \subseteq M$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$ if every subset of $s$ that is an arithmetic progression of length $l$ forces $l \le 1$; equivalently, $l \le 1$ or no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$.

results.title: A progression of length greater than one is not progression-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a set in an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ with $l > 1$. If $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$, then $s$ is not free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$.

results.title: Progression-free finite sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and $l \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. A finite set $s \subseteq M$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $l$ if it is so as a set: $l \le 1$, or no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $l$.

results.title: Sets of naturals without three-term progressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a set of natural numbers such that $a = b$ whenever $a, b, c \in s$ satisfy $a + c = 2b$. Then $s$ is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $3$: no subset of $s$ is an arithmetic progression of length $3$.

results.title: Largest size of a progression-free subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $N$, $r_k(N)$ is the largest cardinality of a subset $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ that is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$, meaning that if $k \ge 2$ then no subset of $S$ is an arithmetic progression of length $k$ (for $k \le 1$ every subset qualifies).

results.title: Trivial upper bound for the largest progression-free subset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $N$, the largest size $r_k(N)$ of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$ satisfies $r_k(N) \le N$.

results.title: A largest progression-free subset is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $N$, let $r_k(N)$ be the largest size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$. Then some subset $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$ has exactly $r_k(N)$ elements.

results.title: Progression-free subsets are bounded by the extremal size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ and $N$ be natural numbers, and let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers with $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ that is free of nontrivial arithmetic progressions of length $k$. Then $|S| \le r_k(N)$, where $r_k(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ containing no nontrivial $k$-term arithmetic progression.

results.title: Set partition
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a finite collection of nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, called blocks, whose union is $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: Crossing in a set partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing if there are $a < b < c < d$ in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $a$ and $c$ lie in the same block of $P$, $b$ and $d$ lie in the same block of $P$, and these two blocks are different.

results.title: Noncrossing set partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is noncrossing if it has no crossing.

results.title: Noncrossing partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A noncrossing partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that is noncrossing.

results.title: Block of a noncrossing partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a noncrossing partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a point $a \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the block of $P$ at $a$ is the block of the underlying set partition that contains $a$.

results.title: Partitions of at most three points are noncrossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \le 3$, every set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is noncrossing.

results.title: Instances of DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH is a quadruple $(n, E, k, m)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges), a natural number $k$ (the size of the vertex set sought) and a natural number $m$ (the edge threshold).

results.title: Well-formed DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, m)$ of DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, with the reversed pair $(v, u)$ not in $E$.

results.title: Feasibility for DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, m)$ of DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH is feasible when there are a finite set $S$ of exactly $k$ natural numbers, each less than $n$, and a sublist $E'$ of $E$ (obtained by deleting entries and keeping the order) with at least $m$ entries such that both components of every pair in $E'$ lie in $S$.

results.title: DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when bitstring decoding of $x$ as a quadruple $(n, E, k, m)$ succeeds and returns an instance of DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH that is both well formed and feasible; every bitstring that does not decode is rejected.

results.title: DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem DENSEST k-SUBGRAPH belongs to the class NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.title: Instances of PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES is a pair consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a list of pairs of natural numbers, the edges.

results.title: Graph of a PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, its graph is the graph of the edge list $E$ on $n$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$. Pairs with an endpoint at least $n$ contribute no edge.

results.title: Well-formed PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers is well formed when $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin E$.

results.title: Partition into triangles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers admits a partition into triangles when the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ can be partitioned into sets of three vertices, any two of which are adjacent in the graph of $E$ on $n$ vertices.

results.title: PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an instance consisting of a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $E$ has no repeated entries, every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin E$, and the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ can be partitioned…

results.title: PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to PARTITION INTO TRIANGLES.

results.title: Multiple-knapsack instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A multiple-knapsack instance consists of a finite list of items, each a pair $(w, v)$ of natural numbers giving its weight $w$ and value $v$, a finite list of natural-number knapsack capacities, and a natural-number target value.

results.title: Feasible multiple-knapsack instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let a multiple-knapsack instance have items $(w_0, v_0), \dots, (w_{k-1}, v_{k-1})$ (weight, value), knapsack capacities $c_0, \dots, c_{m-1}$ and target $V$. The instance is feasible when there are $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1} \in \{0, \dots, m\}$, where $a_j = b < m$ puts item $j$ in knapsack $b$ and $a_j = m$ leaves item $j$ out, such that for every $b < m$ the total weight $\sum_{j : a_j = b} w_j$ is at most $c_b$, and…

results.title: MULTIPLE KNAPSACK as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem MULTIPLE KNAPSACK accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a feasible multiple-knapsack instance. Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.

results.title: MULTIPLE KNAPSACK is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem MULTIPLE KNAPSACK belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to MULTIPLE KNAPSACK.

part.title: Michaelis–Menten kinetics and the quasi-steady state

path: Michaelis–Menten kinetics and the quasi-steady state

results.title: Michaelis constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Michaelis constant `K_M = (kb + k₂)/k₁` (Briggs–Haldane). Meaningful for `k₁ > 0`.

results.title: Mass-action rate of the substrate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mass-action rate of the substrate, `s' = -k₁ e s + kb c`.

results.title: Mass-action rate of the enzyme–substrate complex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mass-action rate of the complex, `c' = k₁ e s - (kb + k₂) c`.

results.title: Solution of the Michaelis–Menten mass-action system
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A solution of the Michaelis–Menten mass-action system on `[0, ∞)`: `s' = -k₁ e s + kb c`, `c' = k₁ e s - (kb + k₂) c`, `e' = -c'`, `p' = k₂ c`.

results.title: Quasi-steady-state value of the complex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The quasi-steady-state value of the complex, `c = e₀ s / (K_M + s)`.

results.title: Michaelis–Menten rate law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Michaelis–Menten rate law `v(s) = V_max s / (K_M + s)`.

results.title: Quasi-steady-state manifold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With total enzyme `e₀` (so `e = e₀ - c`), `k₁ > 0` and `K_M + s ≠ 0`, the complex is stationary iff `c = e₀ s / (K_M + s)`.

results.title: Briggs–Haldane rate law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the quasi-steady-state manifold the product forms at rate `k₂ c = V_max s / (K_M + s)`, `V_max = k₂ e₀`.

results.title: Substrate consumption at the Michaelis–Menten rate under QSSA
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the quasi-steady-state manifold the substrate is consumed at the Michaelis–Menten rate: `s' = -V_max s / (K_M + s)`.

results.title: Michaelis–Menten rate is strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rate law is strictly increasing on `s ≥ 0` for `V_max, K_M > 0`.

results.title: Michaelis constant is the half-saturation substrate level
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Michaelis constant is the half-saturation substrate level: `v(K_M) = V_max / 2`.

results.title: Michaelis–Menten rate stays below its maximum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rate law is below its maximum: `v(s) < V_max` for `s ≥ 0`, `V_max, K_M > 0`.

results.title: Saturation of the Michaelis–Menten rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Saturation: `v(s) → V_max` as `s → ∞`.

results.title: Fast transient of the complex with frozen substrate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The fast transient of the complex with the substrate frozen at `s̄`: `c(t) = c* + (c₀ - c*) e^{-k₁ (s̄ + K_M) t}`, where `c* = e₀ s̄ / (K_M + s̄)`.

results.title: Fast transient solves the boundary-layer equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fast transient solves the boundary-layer equation `c' = k₁ (e₀ - c) s̄ - (kb + k₂) c` for `k₁ > 0` and `K_M + s̄ ≠ 0`.

results.title: Fast transient converges to the quasi-steady state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fast transient converges to the quasi-steady-state value for `k₁ > 0` and `s̄ + K_M > 0`.

results.title: Rigorous QSSA
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Rigorous QSSA (Tikhonov 1952; Heineken–Tsuchiya–Aris 1967). On the slow time scale `τ = e₀ t`, the substrate of the full Michaelis–Menten system with `s(0) = s₀`, `c(0) = 0`, `e(0) = e₀` stays within `C e₀` of the solution `S̄` of the reduced equation `dS̄/dτ = -k₂ S̄ / (K_M + S̄)`, `S̄(0) = s₀`, uniformly on `[0, T]`.
